posts.author: Hereticsys
posts.body: So, I am making an rpg roguelike. And I had an idea using conditional branches and variables to create a sort of pseudo random experience- Where whenever the player enters a new room it runs through randomizing a variable, then sending the player to a room according to what number is picked. For now I set it up with 10 rooms to make sure it's working, and for some reason it's just...not? I click "i'm ready' as i've set up and nothing happens. Does anybody have any tips for maybe streamlining the randomization process to make it less spaghetti, or at the very least figuring out how to get this to work. screenshot of process:

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Note that nesting one branch inside another means "if this AND that". So your logic reads:
If rooms = 1
Transfer to "Room 1"
If rooms = 2 (impossible because rooms = 1!)
(Unreachable commands)
Instead you would want the branches to be separate, or use Else branches. E.g.
If rooms = 1
Transfer to "Room 1"
If rooms = 2
Transfer to "Room 2"
...
Edit: also, if you're actually using RPG Maker MZ then I recommend updating to the latest version.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
I was ninja'd by
@caethyril
above on a rare question that I actually knew the answer too!
But seriously, aside from the nesting issue, are you planning on allowing the player to go backwards or backtrack?
Also, have you thought about how you will make it so the same room doesn't come up again next time?
Regardless, I have an old tutorial for doing Random Transfers. This covers the concept of setting up how to return to where you left and not having duplicates for transfers. Essentially, I took a map with paths exiting North, South, East, and West. When the player chooses a path, the transfer is randomly chosen. The player can then return to the starting map and that first path they chose is now set and locked in so they can go back and forth. As they chose paths, the random transfer options can't be repeated.
I would probably do this differently today, but there might be something useful in it for what you are planning. Or maybe not. Just thought I would share it in case it helps.
Good luck on your projects!
